+from django.test import TestCase
+from .models import (
+    Issue,
+    ProxyTrackerUser,
+    BaseUser,
+    TrackerUser,
+    Improvement,
+    ProxyProxyBug,
+    Bug,
+)
+
+
+class ProxySelectRelatedOnlyTests(TestCase):
+    def test_select_related_only_with_proxy_model(self):
+        """
+        Test that select_related() followed by only() works with proxy models.
+        This is a regression test for the issue where using select_related()
+        and only() together on a proxy model would raise a ValueError.
+        """
+        # Create test data
+        base_user = BaseUser.objects.create(name="Base User")
+        tracker_user = TrackerUser.objects.create(name="Tracker User", status="active")
+        proxy_tracker_user = ProxyTrackerUser.objects.create(
+            name="Proxy Tracker User", status="active"
+        )
+
+        issue = Issue.objects.create(summary="Test Issue", assignee=proxy_tracker_user)
+
+        # This should not raise a ValueError
+        result = list(
+            Issue.objects.select_related("assignee").only("assignee__name").all()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(result[0].summary, "Test Issue")
+        self.assertEqual(result[0].assignee.name, "Proxy Tracker User")
+
+    def test_select_related_only_with_proxy_of_proxy_model(self):
+        """
+        Test that select_related() followed by only() works with proxy of proxy models.
+        This is a regression test for the issue where using select_related()
+        and only() together on a proxy of proxy model would raise a ValueError.
+        """
+        # Create test data
+        base_user = BaseUser.objects.create(name="Base User")
+        proxy_tracker_user = ProxyTrackerUser.objects.create(
+            name="Proxy Tracker User", status="active"
+        )
+        proxy_proxy_bug = ProxyProxyBug.objects.create(
+            summary="Test Bug",
+            assignee=proxy_tracker_user,
+            version="1.0",
+            reporter=base_user,
+        )
+
+        improvement = Improvement.objects.create(
+            summary="Test Improvement",
+            assignee=proxy_tracker_user,
+            version="1.0",
+            reporter=proxy_tracker_user,
+            associated_bug=proxy_proxy_bug,
+        )
+
+        # This should not raise a ValueError
+        result = list(
+            Improvement.objects.select_related("associated_bug").only(
+                "associated_bug__summary"
+            ).all()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(result[0].summary, "Test Improvement")
+        self.assertEqual(result[0].associated_bug.summary, "Test Bug")
+
+    def test_select_related_only_with_proxy_model_fk(self):
+        """
+        Test that select_related() followed by only() works when the FK
+        points to a proxy model.
+        """
+        # Create test data
+        base_user = BaseUser.objects.create(name="Base User")
+        proxy_tracker_user = ProxyTrackerUser.objects.create(
+            name="Proxy Tracker User", status="active"
+        )
+
+        # Bug has a FK to ProxyTrackerUser (through Issue)
+        bug = Bug.objects.create(
+            summary="Test Bug",
+            assignee=proxy_tracker_user,
+            version="1.0",
+            reporter=base_user,
+        )
+
+        # This should not raise a ValueError
+        result = list(
+            Bug.objects.select_related("assignee").only("assignee__name").all()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(result), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(result[0].summary, "Test Bug")
+        self.assertEqual(result[0].assignee.name, "Proxy Tracker User")

+print(f"  Serialized: {result}")

+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+result = MigrationWriter.serialize(combined)
+print(f"  Serialized: {result}")
+
+# Test 3: Round-trip test
+print("\nTest 3: Round-trip test")
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE

+print(f"  Imports: {imports}")
+
+# Execute the serialized code
+d = {}
+exec("\n".join(imports) + "\ntest_value_result = " + string, globals(), d)

+print(f"  Result: {result}")
+print(f"  Expected: {combined}")
+print(f"  Match: {result == combined}")
+
+# Test 4: Test with IntFlagEnum

+

+

+d = {}

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+import re
+import enum
+
+# Test 1: Single flag
+print("Test 1: Single flag")
+print(f"  re.UNICODE: {re.UNICODE}")
+print(f"  Type: {type(re.UNICODE)}")
+print(f"  Has name: {hasattr(re.UNICODE, 'name')}")
+if hasattr(re.UNICODE, 'name'):
+    print(f"  Name: {re.UNICODE.name}")
+
+# Test 2: Combined flags
+print("\nTest 2: Combined flags")
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+print(f"  re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE: {combined}")
+print(f"  Type: {type(combined)}")
+print(f"  Has name: {hasattr(combined, 'name')}")
+if hasattr(combined, 'name'):
+    print(f"  Name: {combined.name}")
+else:
+    print(f"  Name: None (this is the problem!)")
+
+# Test 3: Check enum._decompose
+print("\nTest 3: Check enum._decompose")
+if hasattr(enum, '_decompose'):
+    decomposed = enum._decompose(type(combined), combined)
+    print(f"  Decomposed: {decomposed}")
+    print(f"  Type of decomposed: {type(decomposed)}")
+else:
+    print("  enum._decompose not available")
+
+# Test 4: Check if we can reconstruct the value
+print("\nTest 4: Reconstruct value")
+enum_class = type(combined)
+print(f"  Enum class: {enum_class}")
+print(f"  Enum class module: {enum_class.__module__}")
+print(f"  Enum class qualname: {enum_class.__qualname__}")
+
+# Try to decompose
+if hasattr(enum, '_decompose'):
+    decomposed = enum._decompose(enum_class, combined)
+    print(f"  Decomposed: {decomposed}")
+    
+    # Try to reconstruct
+    if decomposed:
+        names = [m.name for m in decomposed]
+        print(f"  Names: {names}")
+        
+        # Try to reconstruct using OR
+        reconstructed = enum_class[names[0]]
+        for name in names[1:]:
+            reconstructed = reconstructed | enum_class[name]
+        print(f"  Reconstructed: {reconstructed}")

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+import re
+import enum
+
+# Test decomposing the combined flag
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+print(f"Combined value: {combined}")
+print(f"Combined name: {combined.name}")
+
+# Try to decompose manually
+print(f"\nManual decomposition:")
+enum_class = re.RegexFlag
+members = []
+for member in enum_class:
+    if member.value != 0 and (combined.value & member.value) == member.value:
+        # Check if this is a "pure" member (not a combination)
+        # by checking if it's in the original members list
+        if member.name in enum_class.__members__:
+            members.append(member)
+            print(f"  Found: {member.name} = {member.value}")
+
+print(f"\nMembers found: {members}")
+
+# Try to reconstruct
+if members:
+    reconstructed = members[0]
+    for member in members[1:]:
+        reconstructed = reconstructed | member
+    print(f"Reconstructed: {reconstructed}")
+    print(f"Reconstructed == original: {reconstructed == combined}")
+
+# Try a different approach - use the name to decompose
+print(f"\nUsing name decomposition:")
+names = combined.name.split('|')
+print(f"Names: {names}")
+
+# Reconstruct using names
+reconstructed = enum_class[names[0]]
+for name in names[1:]:
+    reconstructed = reconstructed | enum_class[name]
+print(f"Reconstructed: {reconstructed}")
+print(f"Reconstructed == original: {reconstructed == combined}")

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+import re
+from django.db.migrations.writer import MigrationWriter
+
+# Test the original issue: re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+print("Test: re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE")
+combined = re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE
+result = MigrationWriter.serialize(combined)
+print(f"  Serialized: {result}")
+
+# Round-trip test
+string, imports = result
+d = {}
+exec("\n".join(imports) + "\ntest_value_result = " + string, globals(), d)
+result = d["test_value_result"]
+print(f"  Result: {result}")
+print(f"  Expected: {combined}")
+print(f"  Match: {result == combined}")
+
+# Test with a field default
+print("\nTest: Field with combined regex flags")
+from django.db import models
+
+field = models.IntegerField(default=re.UNICODE | re.IGNORECASE)
+result = MigrationWriter.serialize(field)
+print(f"  Serialized: {result[0]}")
+
+# Verify the serialized code is valid
+string = result[0]
+d = {}
+try:
+    exec("from django.db import models\nimport re\n" + string, globals(), d)
+    print(f"  Serialization successful!")
+except Exception as e:
+    print(f"  ERROR: {e}")
